output.summary: No material adversarial findings in the end-to-end release-gate design.
Approved the end-to-end validation and measurement design.

Align end-to-end release gates with committed-only endpoints and ordinary stable-input execution, explicitly deferring worktree and mutation-proof claims. Require both a real v2 conditional sparse case with independently validated context and negative coverage that forces full fallback for missing or altered requirements, alongside reproducible full-run comparisons and timing.
Both reviews approve the integrated release-gate and measurement design. No open findings or notes require verdicts.

findings.impact: The release gate may reject a correctly completed full fallback or incorrectly accept a receipt whose full-run identity is incomplete.
findings.text: The v2 matrix requires missing or incomplete conditional context to trigger a full-profile fallback, but later forbids a full-profile passing receipt for any incomplete context. When a collector is needed only for sparse eligibility yet the original full run and its receipt identity are otherwise valid, those requirements conflict with G2's successful-full-run receipt behavior. Distinguish missing sparse-only conditions from missing context required to validate the full run or its receipt, and test both outcomes.

spec: Exercise the complete product against the release gates and acceptance matrix in docs/test-impact/design.md sections 11, 13 and 14. Add targeted fixtures for the supported ecosystems, including callbacks, reflection, shared fixtures, generated code, resources and cross-project dependencies. Compare selections with full-suite runs on representative histories and deliberately introduced failures, recording limitations and fixing or tracking defects as appropriate. Measure end-to-end snapshot, graph, discovery, setup and execution costs against full runs, selected unit count and fallback frequency. Document reproducible evidence and supported boundaries; do not claim the comparison proves all dependency kinds are modeled. The entire design remains binding. Work directly in this fork for an eventual upstream pull request; no separate product repository or subtree. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
